First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼-1-\frac{16}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=-\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
sin\,((2n-1)\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}))=sin\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-n\pi )=(-1)^{n}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=-\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(-\frac{\pi }{2})=3.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-1-\frac{16}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,((2n-1)\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\ 3 & =-1-\frac{16}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot (-1)^{n} \\ 4 & =-\frac{16}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} & =-\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
